title: I Reported the School Bus Camera After They Denied the Stop Never Happened

parts.text: I waited at the corner at 7:02 a.m. with my third-grader in a red coat. The bus did not stop. It slowed, the driver looked at us, and it rolled. I was thirty-six, late for a shift, holding a thermos. Dispatch said the GPS showed a completed stop. I asked for the camera. They said cameras are not for parents. I filed a safety report with the time, the coat, and a neighbor's doorbell clip of the bus never opening. Then the school marked my kid absent and the attendance office called me about truancy.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They marked her absent after the bus skipped the stop and called it truancy.

social.video_title: The GPS claimed a stop the door never made — Part 1/2
social.description: Red coat, thermos, doorbell clip. Dispatch believed the ping. Then truancy. Would you have driven to school?

parts.text: Transportation reviewed the camera because safety reports outrank the phrase not for parents. The door had not opened. The absence was cleared. The driver was retrained on that corner. I got a written apology that sounded like a template and I accepted it like a template. My kid rode the next day. The coat stayed red. The doorbell still points at the curb. Truancy stayed in a file that now has a clip. GPS is not a door.

social.description: Absence cleared, corner retrained, template apology. Was a roll-by a stop?
